title: Getters and setters
learningObjectives: Explain getters and setters and debug or organise JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: Getters and setters define accessor properties. A getter runs when a property is read; a setter runs when a value is assigned. They can compute derived values or validate assignments, but should not hide expensive work or surprising side effects.
understand.whyItMatters: Accessors can provide a clean property interface while keeping internal representation controlled. Use them carefully so reading a property remains predictable.
understand.analogy: A getter is a read window into a value; a setter is a controlled entry point for updating it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; debugger, module, prototype, and function-call behaviour follow JavaScript and browser runtime rules.

explain.narrative: Reading fullName calculates a value from two fields; assigning it invokes the setter and updates those fields.

examples.explanation: Reading fullName calculates a value from two fields; assigning it invokes the setter and updates those fields.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the code organisation or runtime behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create an object with a getter for a formatted label and a setter that validates a simple value. Explain when each accessor runs.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that uses the feature. Inspect its runtime behaviour and explain the scope, receiver, or call path involved.
hints: Use breakpoints to inspect changing values.
Test methods both through their object and when passed as callbacks.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Getters and setters</title></head><body>
<script>const learner={firstName:'Asha',lastName:'Ali',get fullName(){return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`;},set fullName(value){const parts=value.split(' ');this.firstName=parts[0]||'';this.lastName=parts.slice(1).join(' ');}};learner.fullName='Ravi Kumar';console.log(learner.fullName);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which accessor runs when a property is read?
questions.explanation: A getter is invoked when the accessor property is read.

questions.prompt: What is a useful debugging or architecture practice?
options: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
Assume the code behaves as intended
questions.answer: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
questions.explanation: Reliable debugging and modular design depend on understanding actual execution and dependencies.
